corrections.claimed_speedup: disas-bench charts (bar lengths measured against axis ticks, approximate): Ryzen 9 9950X: bddisasm decode+format 46.8 MB/s, bddisasm mini decode+format 48.8 MB/s, Capstone decode+format 27.5 MB/s; decode-only bddisasm 105.7 MB/s, bddisasm mini 179.3 MB/s. i9-13900K: bddisasm decode+format 35.6 MB/s, mini 39.0 MB/s, Capstone 25.9 MB/s; decode-only 102.7 MB/s, mini 179.5 MB/s. Decode+format ratio to Capstone 1.70x (AMD) and 1.37x (Intel), mini 1.77x and 1.51x (derived from page data, chart readings). README alone: legacy decoder around 240 CPU clocks per decoded instruction (~12M instructions/s) and mini decoder around 150 clocks (~17M instructions/s) on an Intel Core Ultra 7 165H with BDDISASM v3.0, no baseline.
corrections.baseline: Capstone (decode+format throughput); Intel XED, diStorm, iced, yaxpeax-x86, Sleigh and the other listed decoders are measured in the same harness
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Harness binaries are built with cc -O3 (bench/cs/Makefile, bench/xed/Makefile, bench/bddisasm/Makefile; bench/zydis via CMake Release), GCC 13.3 on the AMD run and GCC 14.2 on the Intel run. Libraries: Capstone 5.0.6 (submodule accf4df) built with its own Makefile, default CFLAGS -O3, CAPSTONE_ARCHS=x86; bddisasm v3.0.0 via CMake Release with BDD_LTO=ON; Zydis via CMake Release (bench/zydis/CMakeLists.txt, submodule 569320a); XED via mfile.py --opt=3 (make-all.sh).
corrections.caveats: Smaller win than iced, yaxpeax-x86 and diStorm in the same charts (iced and yaxpeax decode+format are about 3.4-5.4x faster than bddisasm); the README's own throughput numbers carry no baseline. Each tool is timed in a single run (clock() CPU time over 20 passes of the 0x2460400-byte code section of a checked-in Firefox xul.dll), with no repetitions or variance reported. disas-bench is maintained by Joel Hoener (athre0z), a Zydis copyright holder; the AMD chart was produced by iximeow (yaxpeax-x86 author, 2025-10-24) and the Intel chart by athre0z (2025-10-26). Chart values are bar lengths read off PNGs against the axis ticks (approximate, about +/-1 MB/s), not a text table. Capstone appears only as a decode+format row (cs_disasm_iter, detail off), so decode+format rows are the like-for-like comparison; formatted text differs in detail between libraries. The bddisasm v3.0.0 update and the mini-decoder rows were contributed to disas-bench by ianichitei (2025-10-10), who also authored earlier bddisasm updates there.

notes: Record accurate; chart readings re-measured from the PNG pixels match the record within rounding (1.70x AMD, 1.37x Intel vs Capstone on decode+format). Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 1.1k stars, 120 forks, not a fork or archived, last commit 2026-10-07 (active). Shortcomings: modest win, slower than iced/yaxpeax/diStorm, single-run timings, suite owner co-authored Zydis.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed OOPSLA 2024 paper (Distinguished Paper; PACMPL 8 OOPSLA2 Article 326 per snippets) whose abstract reports speedups over clang -O3; the paper (arXiv 2306.00229, par.nsf.gov, deepai, llvm.org slides) was blocked, so the numbers and venue come from search snippets only, and the repo has no benchmark code or numbers, so not A.

corrections.baseline: clang/LLVM -O3 without the Minotaur pass (per search snippets of the paper)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper abstract, seen via search snippets only (paper not opened): on an Intel Cascade Lake processor, GMP benchmark suite mean speedup 7.3% (max 13%) and SPEC CPU 2017 mean speedup 1.5% (max 4.5% on 638.imagick) over clang -O3. Single snippets also give a 1.2% SPEC mean on AMD and a LibYUV geomean of 1.029x on AMD Zen 3; a summary of an older paper version gives different LibYUV figures, so those two are unconfirmed.
corrections.hardware: Intel Cascade Lake (GMP and SPEC headline numbers); AMD Zen 3 for LibYUV and the compile-time tables per snippets; exact CPU models not seen
corrections.caveats: All numbers come from search-result text of the paper (arXiv 2306.00229 v3, OOPSLA 2024); the paper, the NSF PAR copy, the deepai mirror and the 2022 LLVM Dev Meeting slides were all blocked, so methodology, flags and exact CPU models were not checked. The repo README has no performance numbers and no evaluation scripts (scripts/ holds only cache and compiler-wrapper tools). Gains on SPEC are small (1.2-1.5% mean). Per snippets, cold-cache builds can be hundreds of times slower than plain -O3 and warm-cache SPEC builds about 3% slower. Using it needs a patched LLVM (llvm-main-minotaur.patch) built with RTTI and exceptions, Alive2, Z3 and a redis server. It is an LLVM IR superoptimizer, so only loosely 'assembly tooling'.

notes: Kept at B on the peer-reviewed paper (same footing as the wave 12 TPDE entry); headline 7.3% GMP and 1.5% SPEC confirmed by several snippets, AMD and LibYUV figures by one snippet each. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 138 stars, 16 forks, not a fork, last commit 2026-01-07 on dev (active). Add to the paper-access retier list (arXiv 2306.00229; two zenodo records surfaced in an artifact search but could not be opened).
